title: Edge-case data retention scenarios and approval plan
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working sketch for uncommon/edge-case retention requests we encountered during the Acme Health POC (week of 2025-11-03). Goal: capture concrete options that satisfy (1) customer regulatory constraints, (2) engineering feasibility across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and (3) minimal legal exposure for Redwood.

Audience: SEs running customer workshops, Solutions leads preparing DPA addenda, and Legal for sign-off.

Summary of customer ask that triggered this doc:
- Customer: Acme Health (clinical SaaS) asked for: 1) absolute no-permanent-storage of PII from inference inputs; 2) ability to run short rollbacks if model outputs need review; 3) exportable audit trail for 90 days; 4) on-demand bulk purge by customer admin.
- Constraints: customer must remain in Hosted for now; cannot accept on-prem deployment before pilot end.

Problem framing (edge cases we've seen):
- Long-tail transcripts: long multi-turn chat sessions that exceed usual KV-cache assumptions and create intermediate artifacts in storage/backups.
- Mixed telemetry: customer wants telemetry for billing/SLAs but not content telemetry tied to PII.
- Asynchronous tooling: files ingested by secondary analysis pipelines (embedding indexers) creating extra copies we must account for.
- Legal-evidence retention: customers sometimes request we keep a tamper-evident copy for 180+ days for dispute resolution.

High-level options (ranked by least-to-most-engineering impact):
1) Ephemeral inference mode (E-mode) - immediate-in-memory only: requests are processed without writing request/response to any long-lived store; KV cache allowed in-memory for active session only; no logs of content except a stub metadata row for billing.
   - Pros: aligns with strict no-storage ask; low legal exposure.
   - Cons: complicates debugging; increases cost if repeated identical requests occur; cannot provide a customer-side 90-day audit trail.

2) Encrypted short-term retention w/ customer key (EKS mode) - store encrypted blobs for a configurable TTL (e.g., 7-90 days), encrypted with customer KMS key (Hosted KMS integration), with automatic purging at TTL expiry.
   - Pros: meets moderate audit/rollback needs; customer retains key control to some degree.
   - Cons: Hosted KMS integration and proof-of-delete semantics required; still stored in our infra.

3) Export-to-cust-s3 after N days (Export mode) - keep minimal metadata for X days to allow tracing, then export full payloads to customer-controlled S3 bucket and purge local copies.
   - Pros: moves long-term custody to customer; satisfies regulatory customers wanting self-controlled evidence stores.
   - Cons: requires customer infra; introduces outbound transfer scheduling and failure mode handling.

4) Escrowed-hash + audit-only storage (Hash-escrow) - retain only salted hashes and metadata in our index, store raw in a secure escrow (third-party or Dedicated vault) only when requested by subpoena or signed request.
   - Pros: minimal data surface, supports dispute workflows.
   - Cons: legal coordination needed; third-party escrow setup complexity.

Technical details and implementation notes (for SEs):
- Ephemeral mode specifics:
  - Disable request/response journaling pipeline (log-forwarder off for session).
  - Ensure KV cache is pinned to node memory and cleared on session termination (explicit call or TTL).
  - Disable embedding pipelines, rerankers that materialize indices.
  - Billing stub must include request token counts and model id, but redact text.
  - Operational SRE hooks: allow debug dump only when customer-signed debug consent exists (stored as signed URL or ticket).

- Encrypted short-term retention specifics:
  - Use customer-supplied KMS key where possible (Hosted KMS CMK envelope encryption).
  - Tag objects with retention metadata: origin-session-id, customer-org-id, TTL-expiry-time, retention-justification.
  - Implement time-based purge job with attestations logged (delete job + removal confirmation written to immutable audit log).
  - Provide API for customer-initiated immediate purge; returns job id + timestamp.

- Export-to-cust-s3 specifics:
  - Handshake flow: customer provides S3 upload role and pre-signed bucket location or cross-account role.
  - Export scheduler runs nightly with retry policy and verifies checksum before local delete.
  - If transfer fails x retries, auto-escalate to Alert team and pause auto-deletion until manual intervention.

- Hash-escrow specifics:
  - Hash scheme: H = SHA256(salt || request-id || canonicalized-payload). Salt stored in HSM; canonicalization rules documented in annex.
  - Escrow vendor options: (1) LegalTrust Vault (review needed), (2) Customer-owned cold archive.

Telemetry separation (recommended pattern):
- Split telemetry streams: (A) billing/usage (tokens, model, latency) kept as normal; (B) content telemetry (prompt/response traces) only stored if customer consents or if in Encrypted short-term retention mode.
- Masking step: pre-ingest redaction pipeline that can pseudonymize names, IDs, PHI patterns according to detection heuristics (Regex + ML-based detectors).
- Default for strict PII customers: enable pattern masking + Ephemeral mode.

DPA addendum language snippets (working drafts - legal please review):
- Minimal retention clause (example): "For the duration of the Pilot, Provider will process Customer Data in Ephemeral Mode, defined as in-memory processing without persistence to durable storage. Provider will maintain only non-content billing metadata required to compute charges. Customer may opt into a Temporary Retention mode (7–90 days) by supplying a KMS key and explicit consent via the API."

- Right-to-delete and attestations clause (example): "Customer may request deletion of Customer Data at any time via the Provider API. Provider shall initiate purge within 24 hours and complete deletion within 72 hours of successful purge initiation, and shall provide a signed deletion attestation referencing the purge job id."

- Export clause (example): "Upon Customer request, Provider will export Customer Data to a Customer-owned storage endpoint (S3 or equivalent) within 7 days and thereafter purge Provider copies after successful verification."

Operational playbook (workshop checklist) - SEs to run with customer:
1) Kickoff: capture regulatory requirements, max retention window, and who signs purge/export requests. (owner: SE)
2) Decide mode: Ephemeral / Encrypted-TTL / Export / Hash-escrow. (owner: SE + Customer Security)
3) If KMS requested: run KMS connectivity test. Save encryption handshake logs. (owner: Infra lead)
4) Telemetry: which traces are allowed? Configure redaction and sampling. (owner: Observability)
5) Test plan: run a 48-hour simulated attack/compromise and validate purge. Log outcomes. (owner: SRE)
6) Legal sign-off: draft addendum and capture SLA around deletion attestations. (owner: Solutions + Legal)
7) Post-pilot handover: export keys, logs, and residual artifacts or certify purge. (owner: Customer Success)

Open questions and action items (for team):
- Q1: What is acceptable proof-of-delete for Legal? Current suggestion: signed attestation with delete-job-id + checksum (Anna to confirm).
- Q2: Can Hosted use customer-supplied CMKs in our Hosted region for short pilots without major infra change? (Priya to scope infra work).
- Q3: Should we support pseudo-anonymization as a first-class POC option (i.e., client-side SDK transformations)? Pros: reduces infra burden; Cons: shifts liability. (SE breakout).
- Q4: Add escrow vendor evaluation to Q1 vendor list; is LegalTrust acceptable? (Anna + Marco).

Draft timelines (rough):
- 1 week: finalize workshop checklist + redaction heuristics
- 2–3 weeks: implement Ephemeral Mode knobs for pilot (toggle config + SRE guardrails)
- 4–6 weeks: build short-term encrypted retention flow + KMS test harness (if customer chooses TTL mode)

Immediate next steps (this doc):
- Leah: schedule a 60-min workshop with Acme Health security lead, include Priya and Anna.
- Ethan: prototype Ephemeral Mode toggles on staging and run purge-attestation script. Link: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/ephemeral-purge-attest
- Anna: provide feedback on addendum snippets above by EOD next Tue.

Notes to self / SE tips:
- Always capture the exact actor who can request purge/export (name + email + corporate ID). That identity will be used in audit trail.
- Keep example payloads small for demos (1–2 short conversations) to avoid accidental materialization during slide decks.
- When in doubt, prefer export-to-customer over long-term retention in Hosted.

References and resources:
- Internal playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Privacy/Retention-Playbook (WIP)
- Ticket for escrow experiment: JIRA-SEC-277
- Related POC docs: sandboxed-pilot-data-strategy-notes.json (see shared drives)

End of notes.
